title: Finite affine cover bound from affine-local restriction acyclicity
statement: Let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec} A$ be separated, with $A$ commutative, and let $i:Z\to X$ be any morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $J$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Assume that for every affine open $W\subseteq X$ and every $k>0$, $H^k(W\times_X Z,(J|_W)|_{W\times_X Z})=0$, using inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and underlying abelian cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. If $X$ has an affine open cover indexed by $\operatorname{Fin}(n+1)$, then $H^q(Z,i^{-1}J)=0$ for every $q>n$. No injectivity, torsion, or closed-immersion assumption is made.

source.place: Proof, Mayer-Vietoris induction (step 6 of the parent node)

proof.text: Induct on n simultaneously for all schemes X and Z over the fixed affine base and all morphisms and sheaves satisfying hlocal. For n = 0, the only affine open is top. Apply hlocal there. The pullback second projection is an isomorphism; use inverse-image composition, the pullback commutativity relation, module-forgetting and topological invariance to transport vanishing back to Z.

In the successor case split off W = U 0 and let V be the union of the remaining n+1 affine opens. Fin.cases proves W ⊔ V = top. Preimages of the remaining affine opens under V.ι are affine by IsAffineOpen.preimage_of_isOpenImmersion and form a cover of V.

The intersections W ∩ U(j.succ) are affine by isAffineHom_diagonal_iff: separatedness of f makes its diagonal a closed immersion and hence affine. These opens lie in W ∩ V; their preimages cover that open scheme, by distributivity and preimage_iSup.

Use the open-restriction inheritance theorem on V and W ∩ V. The induction hypothesis, which now quantifies over these open schemes and their pullback schemes, gives the degree q vanishing on V and degree q-1 vanishing on the intersection. The chosen affine W has positive-degree vanishing directly from hlocal.
Write q = r+1. From n+1 < q infer n < q and n < r. Apply the two-open module-pullback Mayer--Vietoris vanishing theorem to W,V with the three vanishing hypotheses.

proof_origin.place: Mayer--Vietoris induction with explicit affine-local acyclicity; Lean proves the base case, cover splitting, affine intersections and induction, leaving only restriction inheritance and two-open vanishing
